nodes.name: Paper editorial
nodes.summary: Warm off-white canvas that reads like paper, a serif display face over a quiet sans, hairline rules, one restrained accent.

nodes.name: Swiss grid
nodes.summary: Black, white and one accent on a visible grid; type does the work, nothing is decorated.

nodes.name: Monochrome engineering
nodes.summary: Greys with colour only where it means something, one sans for everything and mono for code, borders that are earned.
tells_to_avoid: mono for anything that is not data

nodes.name: Soft product
nodes.summary: Friendly product UI: large radius, soft layered shadows, a clear primary, airy cards, pill buttons.
tells_to_avoid: the same grey shadow under everything

nodes.name: Dark console
nodes.summary: Near-black neutral surfaces, hairline borders, mono labels for data, one restrained accent; the look of a good terminal.
tells_to_avoid: medium grey body text on black

nodes.name: Luminous dark
nodes.summary: Dark canvas with one glowing hue, blurred gradient light, glassy raised panels and product imagery doing the talking.

nodes.name: Quiet luxury
nodes.summary: Generous space, a refined serif, muted low-chroma palette, square corners and almost no chrome.

nodes.name: Neo-brutalist
nodes.summary: Flat saturated fills, thick dark borders, hard offset shadows, raw grotesque type; deliberately unpolished.

nodes.name: Playful geometric
nodes.summary: Bright flat colour blocks, geometric shapes, pill everything, bouncy motion; made to be liked.

nodes.name: Warm organic
nodes.summary: Earth tones, rounded forms, generous line height, photography with large radius; calm and human.
tells_to_avoid: cream and terracotta as a default

nodes.name: Glass layered
nodes.summary: Translucent panels over a coloured field, blur used only where a surface really floats over content.

nodes.name: Bento showcase
nodes.summary: A grid of unequal cells, each showing one real product capability with a small mono caption.
tells_to_avoid: cells with icons instead of product

nodes.name: Poster type
nodes.summary: Display type at poster scale is the image; everything else is small, aligned and quiet.
tells_to_avoid: one word in a different colour
italic serif as the only idea

nodes.name: Sand & Indigo

nodes.name: Hazard Yellow
nodes.notes: Flat hazard yellow with black text and a red secondary; in light mode the primary is a deeper ochre-yellow so it reads on white, the full hazard yellow lives in dark mode and large fills; neo-brutalist and poster layouts.

nodes.name: Sky & Tomato
nodes.notes: Bright sky blue primary with a tomato accent on cool white; playful geometric, kids, consumer apps.

nodes.name: Poppy & Cream
nodes.notes: Poppy red-orange primary with a leaf-green accent on cream; playful retail, food delivery, brutalist menus.

nodes.name: Fraunces / Figtree
nodes.notes: Fraunces' soft old-style curves carry the personality at display sizes while Figtree stays quiet and even in running text; keep Fraunces upright and under 64px to avoid the oversized-italic-serif tell.

nodes.name: Instrument Serif / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: Drawn as a family, the condensed high-contrast serif and the neutral grotesque share proportions, so headlines feel sharp without the body fighting them; use the roman, not the italic, for H1.

nodes.name: Newsreader / Source Sans 3
nodes.notes: Newsreader's optical-size axis keeps headlines crisp and decks readable, and Source Sans 3's humanist rhythm matches its transitional body shapes for long-form reading.

nodes.name: Source Serif 4 / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Two workhorse faces with matched x-heights: Source Serif 4 gives documents authority, Public Sans keeps UI and forms plain and legible, the kind of pairing legal and fintech products can trust.

nodes.name: Libre Caslon Text / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Caslon's sturdy old-style forms give headlines a printed-book weight and Work Sans, an early-grotesque revival, is period-adjacent without competing in texture.

nodes.name: Playfair Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: A Didone headline needs a low-contrast geometric body, which DM Sans supplies; the classic magazine contrast works because the sans has no calligraphic stress to argue with (never swap in a humanist sans).

nodes.name: Cormorant Garamond / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cormorant's small x-height and long extenders read as refinement at large sizes, and Hanken Grotesk's plain, slightly narrow grotesque recedes so the serif and the whitespace carry the page.

nodes.name: Literata / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Literata was drawn for long screen reading and its optical sizes keep headlines from going spindly; Albert Sans adds a soft geometric counterpoint for UI labels without stealing attention.

nodes.name: Lora / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Lora's brushy, moderate-contrast serif and Nunito Sans' rounded humanist forms share a gentle calligraphic stress, so the pairing feels warm and organic rather than corporate.

nodes.name: EB Garamond / Onest
nodes.notes: Old-style Garamond and a humanist sans descend from the same broad-nib stress, so unlike Didone + humanist this is harmonious; Onest's slightly larger x-height keeps body copy modern.

nodes.name: Young Serif / Rethink Sans
nodes.notes: Young Serif's heavy, low-contrast letterforms behave like a display face so one weight is enough; Rethink Sans' clean geometry keeps the page from tipping into kitsch.

nodes.name: Gloock / Manrope
nodes.notes: Gloock is a single-weight Didone built for poster sizes, so pair it with Manrope's even geometric strokes at 1.414 scale and keep it to one or two lines per page; a humanist body would clash with its vertical stress.

nodes.name: DM Serif Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: Designed as siblings, DM Serif Display's Scotch-roman contrast and DM Sans' low-contrast geometry share a skeleton, which is why the heading and body feel like one voice at two volumes.

nodes.name: Inter Tight / Inter
nodes.notes: Inter Tight gives the headline the tight tracking Inter lacks at display sizes so the family stops looking like an unchosen default; only use it with a distinct accent colour and real product imagery.

nodes.name: Geist / Geist
nodes.notes: One sans for everything with Geist Mono reserved for code, paths and IDs is the Vercel design.md recipe; the discipline is in the restraint, not the face.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Figtree
nodes.notes: Bricolage's optical-size axis turns on its wonky display details only at headline sizes, and Figtree's smooth geometry below it keeps the quirk from infecting the reading text.

nodes.name: Schibsted Grotesk / Inter
nodes.notes: A newspaper grotesque with real character at headline sizes over Inter at text sizes gives a Swiss-grid page two distinct voices without leaving the grotesque family.

nodes.name: Plus Jakarta Sans / Plus Jakarta Sans
nodes.notes: A single geometric family at two weights is the quietest way to get a soft product voice; the slightly rounded terminals read friendly without needing pill-shaped type tricks.

nodes.name: Outfit / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Outfit's pure circles and verticals suit bright colour blocks and big rounded cards, and Nunito Sans softens the body copy so the page stays likeable rather than cold.

nodes.name: Sora / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Sora's wide, slightly squared geometry reads as technical on a dark canvas, and Work Sans' plainer grotesque keeps paragraphs neutral under glow and glass effects.

nodes.name: Host Grotesk / Funnel Sans
nodes.notes: Two 2024-25 Google releases nobody has defaulted to yet: Host Grotesk's compact grotesque headlines over Funnel Sans' open geometric text avoid the Inter-everywhere tell while staying strictly neutral.

nodes.name: Chivo / Be Vietnam Pro
nodes.notes: Chivo's heavy grotesque weights give headlines the punch a visible grid wants, and Be Vietnam Pro's cleaner neo-grotesque keeps body text from going muddy at small sizes.

nodes.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next / Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
nodes.notes: Built for low-vision readers with unambiguous glyphs, this family at two weights is the safe choice for dense tables and forms where character confusion costs money.

nodes.name: Archivo / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo's width axis lets the heading run condensed and heavy while the body stays normal width, so one grotesque does both jobs on a visible grid with hard edges.

nodes.name: Roboto Flex / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Flex's optical-size and grade axes keep 12px table text and 40px titles equally crisp, and its tabular figures line up in tight rows; one variable file covers the whole dashboard.

nodes.name: Manrope / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Manrope's rounded geometric headlines carry the product personality and IBM Plex Sans' slightly engineered grotesque keeps settings pages and forms businesslike underneath.

nodes.name: JetBrains Mono / Inter
nodes.notes: Mono headlines at a modest 1.2 scale read like a good terminal prompt rather than a gimmick, and Inter below them keeps prose and tables legible on near-black surfaces.

nodes.name: IBM Plex Mono / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Plex Mono and Plex Sans share widths and weights, so mono headings, sans prose and mono data columns align on the same baseline grid without visual seams.

nodes.name: Geist Mono / Geist
nodes.notes: Leading with Geist Mono for titles and captions and dropping to Geist for sentences gives bento cells and dark consoles a data-first voice while staying one coherent superfamily.

nodes.name: Space Mono / Space Grotesk
nodes.notes: Space Mono's quirky retro terminals make a deliberately unpolished headline, and Space Grotesk (its proportional sibling) carries the same DNA; reserve it for brutalist pages since Space Grotesk alone is now a default tell.

nodes.name: Martian Mono / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Martian Mono's width axis gives compact mono headers and labels that sit over dense tables, and Public Sans' neutral neo-grotesque handles the surrounding UI copy.

nodes.name: Azeret Mono / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Azeret Mono is a chunky display mono built to be set large with thick borders and hard shadows, and Albert Sans' plain geometry keeps the body copy from adding more noise.

nodes.name: Syne / Manrope
nodes.notes: Syne's extended heavy weights are the image at poster scale, so everything else is small Manrope aligned to the grid; one headline per screen is the rule.

nodes.name: Unbounded / Onest
nodes.notes: Unbounded's ultra-wide geometric display letters fill a hero on their own; Onest's compact humanist body is the counterweight that keeps the rest of the page readable.

nodes.name: Archivo Black / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo Black is the fat grotesque neo-brutalism wants for flat fills and thick borders, and regular Archivo is literally the same design at text weight so the hierarchy is seamless.

nodes.name: Anton / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Anton's tall condensed caps pack a long headline into a tight block, and Work Sans' wider grotesque text opens the page back up beneath it; set Anton tight and never in italic.

nodes.name: Clash Display / Satoshi
nodes.notes: Clash Display's wide, slightly squared display forms give poster-type headlines a distinct 2020s brand voice, and Satoshi (same foundry) is a neutral geometric that stays out of the way; self-host both via Fontshare.

nodes.name: Cal Sans / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cal Sans is the single-weight display face Cal.com ships for headlines; over Hanken Grotesk's plain text it gives a product page a clear, non-default headline voice at low cost.

nodes.name: Roboto Slab / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Slab and Roboto Flex share a skeleton, so slab headings over a flexible neo-grotesque body give documentation and dense admin pages structure without any stylistic seam.

nodes.name: Zilla Slab / Lato
nodes.notes: Zilla Slab's soft slab serifs (Mozilla's brand face) and Lato's warm humanist sans both have a slight calligraphic warmth, so the pairing feels approachable rather than mechanical.

nodes.name: Bitter / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Bitter was drawn as a reading slab for screens, so its headings stay soft and even, and Hanken Grotesk's quiet grotesque body keeps long articles calm.

nodes.name: System UI / System UI
nodes.notes: Zero font requests and native rendering on every platform; the right call for app shells, glass companions and data tools where the OS face is the honest choice.

nodes.name: System Serif / System Sans
nodes.fallback_heading: ui-serif, 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif
nodes.notes: New York on Apple and Georgia elsewhere give an editorial headline with no webfont cost, over the platform sans; useful for content sites that must be fast on first paint.

nodes.name: Studio wrap
nodes.summary: A pale neutral canvas, one giant grotesque headline with alternating indents wrapping a single flat disc of saturated colour, square corners, almost no chrome; a designer's own site, not a product template.

nodes.name: Lab figures
nodes.summary: Near-black lab notebook: line-art isometric figures with mono captions (Fig 0.1), a two-tone statement paragraph instead of a headline and buttons, hairline column rules.

nodes.name: Split nav with live metadata
nodes.what: Navigation reduced to three things: the wordmark left, a mono line in the centre with the studio's city and local time ticking each second, and a single word 'Menu' on the right. No link row, no button.
nodes.implementation: Three-column grid; centre cell is mono 11px with letter-spacing .06em; a 1s setInterval updates the time; the menu word toggles an overlay.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Live metadata is specific to the owner and never appears in generated sites.

nodes.name: Menu word and full-screen overlay
nodes.what: The nav holds only the wordmark and the word 'Menu'. Clicking it opens a full-viewport overlay in the ink colour with four to six links at display size, each entering with an 80ms stagger, and a 'Close' word where 'Menu' was.
nodes.implementation: A dialog element or a fixed div with role=dialog; links at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem); transform translateY(20px) to 0 with ease-out over 500ms; Escape closes; respect reduced motion by fading only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites always show the link row; a word-only nav reads as designed.

nodes.name: Floating pill nav
nodes.what: A compact pill detached from the top edge by 16px, centred, holding the wordmark and three links, with a blurred backdrop only once content scrolls under it.
nodes.implementation: position: sticky; top: 16px; width: max-content; margin-inline: auto; border-radius: 999px; backdrop-filter: blur(12px) applied with a scroll-driven animation or a class toggled after 40px of scroll.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common on 2024 Framer templates; acceptable on soft product sites, avoid elsewhere.

nodes.name: Numbered index rail
nodes.what: A thin left rail with section numbers 01 to 05 in mono; the current section's number is in text colour, the rest muted; clicking jumps. The main nav is a single line at the top.
nodes.implementation: position: fixed; left: 24px; top: 50%; translate: 0 -50%; IntersectionObserver sets aria-current; hidden under 1024px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rails tied to real sections show structure, which templates do not have.

nodes.name: Giant word ticker hero
nodes.what: The first screen is the brand name or a two-word claim at 18 to 22vw, repeated as a single-line marquee that moves at about 60px per second, with one sentence and one link set small beneath it.
nodes.implementation: A flex track duplicated once, animation: translateX(-50%) linear 40s infinite; prefers-reduced-motion pauses it; font-size clamp(5rem, 20vw, 22rem); line-height .8; letter-spacing -.05em.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A marquee of logos is a tell; a single giant moving word as the hero is a studio move, keep it to one.

nodes.name: Type specimen hero
nodes.what: The headline is presented like a foundry specimen: the sentence at display size with mono metadata around it (face name, size in px, weight, the date), hairlines above and below, and the alphabet or numerals in a strip beneath.
nodes.implementation: Grid with mono labels at 11px in the corners; display line at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 8rem); a second row with 0123456789 in tabular numerals at 24px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specimen furniture requires a real face choice and real values.

nodes.name: Manifesto hero
nodes.what: The first screen is one paragraph of 60 to 120 words at 28 to 44px, left aligned, with no headline and no buttons; a single inline link closes the paragraph. The paragraph says what the company believes, in first person plural.
nodes.implementation: max-width 34ch to 40ch; font-size clamp(1.6rem, 3vw, 2.75rem); line-height 1.2; text-wrap: pretty; margin-top 20vh.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Needs real prose; the template cannot fake it.

nodes.name: Three numbers hero
nodes.what: Three large numerals (96 to 160px, tabular) with a one-line caption each, set as the first screen; the product name is only in the nav. The numbers are sourced claims, never invented.
nodes.implementation: Grid of three; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; captions mono 11px; count-up once when in view if motion is on.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invented numbers are the tell; sourced ones are the proof.

nodes.name: Type larger than the viewport
nodes.what: The headline is set so large that its first and last letters bleed past the viewport edges; what remains legible is the middle of the word, and a small subhead sits in the exposed corner.
nodes.implementation: font-size clamp(8rem, 28vw, 30rem); white-space: nowrap; margin-inline: -0.12em; overflow-x: clip on the section; line-height .78.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only a confident brand crops its own name; templates centre it.

nodes.name: Stacked words in alternating faces
nodes.what: Three to four words of the headline stacked one per line, alternating between the heading face solid and the same face outlined, or between the grotesque and a serif, with a hard left edge.
nodes.implementation: display: grid; each span line-height .9; outline lines use -webkit-text-stroke: 1px currentColor; color: transparent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Serif-italic alternation is now common on templates; outline alternation reads fresher.

nodes.name: Marquee divider line
nodes.what: Between two sections, a single line of mono text (the real client list, the product nouns or the location and year) slides slowly, 40 seconds per loop, separated by small marks, pausing on hover.
nodes.implementation: Track duplicated once; animation 40s linear infinite; mono 12px uppercase off (sentence case), separators as 4px squares in primary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Logo marquees are a tell; a slow mono text line with real words reads as a studio device.

nodes.name: Giant numerals index
nodes.what: Features or services listed with 01, 02, 03 set at 120 to 200px in muted ink (8 to 12 percent alpha) behind or beside a title and one sentence; hairline between rows.
nodes.implementation: Each row a grid: numeral column 1fr with font-size clamp(5rem, 12vw, 12rem) colour color-mix(text 10%); tabular nums; title at 2xl.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Numbers as the composition rather than as a tiny decoration.

nodes.name: Sticky stacking cards
nodes.what: Three to five full-width cards each sticky at the top; as the page scrolls, the next card slides over the previous one leaving a 16px lip of the earlier cards visible, each with its own surface colour.
nodes.implementation: Each card position: sticky; top: calc(96px + var(--i) * 16px); min-height 70vh; later cards get a slightly darker surface; no JS.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Frequent on Framer templates; works when each card holds a real product state.

nodes.name: Horizontal scroll strip
nodes.what: A row of cards or images that scrolls sideways with scroll snap; the last item is cut by the viewport edge so the overflow is obvious; a mono count '03 / 08' sits above.
nodes.implementation: display: flex; overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; gap 16px; padding-inline-end 25vw; scrollbar hidden; each child scroll-snap-align: start.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Needs real items with different weights; the cut edge is the point.

nodes.name: Hover list with image reveal
nodes.what: Work or features as plain rows (title left, meta right, hairline between). Hovering a row reveals an image that follows the cursor with a 120ms lag; on touch the image sits beside the row.
nodes.implementation: A fixed img element positioned from pointermove with translate3d and a lerp of .12 per frame; rows carry data-image; reduced motion shows the image statically on the right.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The standard studio portfolio list since 2022, never generated by default.

nodes.name: Bordered cells with corner crosses
nodes.what: Content sits in a grid of cells divided by 1px hairlines in text colour at 10 percent alpha, with small plus marks (12px) drawn at the intersections; cells have different spans.
nodes.implementation: Grid with gap 1px and background set to the hairline colour; each cell background bg; crosses are absolutely positioned pseudo-elements at the cell corners.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The engineering grid of Vercel and Linear changelogs; the crosses are the signature.

nodes.name: Hairline accordion
nodes.what: Questions or services as hairline rows; a plus sign at the right rotates 45 degrees to a cross when open; the open row's answer sits at the reading measure; only one open at a time.
nodes.implementation: details and summary elements; summary::after content '+' in mono; transition rotate 200ms; name attribute groups them for exclusive open (Chrome 120, Safari 17.2).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rows with a plus, not cards with a chevron.

nodes.name: One giant quote
nodes.what: One attributed quote at 40 to 64px in the heading face with hanging punctuation, the opening mark outdented into the margin, and a small attribution line; no carousel, no avatars.
nodes.implementation: hanging-punctuation: first (Safari) with a text-indent fallback of -0.4em; font-size clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 4rem); max-width 24ch.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A carousel of three invented testimonials is the tell; one real quote at scale is the opposite.

nodes.name: Stat wall
nodes.what: A full-width row of three or four sourced figures at 96px or larger in tabular numerals, each with a one-line label and a footnote number that links to the source.
nodes.implementation: Grid of equal columns with hairline dividers; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; sup elements link to a sources list in the footer.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only sourced figures; otherwise this is the invented-stats tell.

nodes.name: Ticket call to action
nodes.what: The closing call to action is drawn as a ticket: a bordered strip with a perforated left edge, a mono meta line (date, seat, price or version) and the single action on the stub.
nodes.implementation: A bordered box with a dashed vertical rule; perforation via radial-gradient mask on the left edge; mono labels 11px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A physical metaphor tied to real data (release date, plan price).

nodes.name: Colophon footer
nodes.what: A one-line footer in mono: the brand, the year, local time, coordinates of the studio, 'set in <face>', the version or commit hash, and the real links. Nothing else.
nodes.implementation: A single flex row at 11px mono with gap 24px wrapping; time via setInterval; version string injected at build.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Real metadata about the real site.

nodes.name: Film grain overlay
nodes.what: A fixed, full-viewport layer of monochrome noise at 4 to 8 percent opacity over the whole page, which kills the flat digital look and binds colours together.
nodes.implementation: An SVG with feTurbulence baseFrequency .9 numOctaves 3 as a background on a fixed div, pointer-events none, mix-blend-mode multiply on light and screen on dark; or a tiny PNG tile.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rare on generated sites, common on studio and dark product sites.

nodes.name: Graph paper grid
nodes.what: A 24 or 32px background grid in text colour at 5 to 7 percent alpha behind the hero or the whole page, fading out at the edges.
nodes.implementation: background-image: linear-gradient(hairline 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, hairline 1px, transparent 1px); background-size 32px 32px; mask-image radial-gradient for the fade.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common on developer tools; keep the alpha low and the grid honest to the layout gutters.

nodes.name: Crosses at grid intersections
nodes.what: Small plus marks, 10 to 12px, drawn where section gutters meet, instead of full grid lines.
nodes.implementation: Pseudo-elements with two 1px bars; placed at section corners via position absolute; colour text at 30 percent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The Vercel and Geist signature; hand-placed marks, not a pattern.

nodes.name: Scanlines
nodes.what: Repeating 2px horizontal lines at 6 to 10 percent alpha over dark imagery or a dark hero, giving a CRT register without a glow.
nodes.implementation: background: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 2px, rgb(0 0 0 / .12) 2px 3px) on an overlay; disable under 420px wide.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tied to hardware and terminal brands; never a default.

nodes.name: Outlined giant word
nodes.what: One word of the display line is drawn as a 1px outline in text colour with a transparent fill, next to solid words; the outlined word is the one the sentence hinges on.
nodes.implementation: span { -webkit-text-stroke: 1px currentColor; color: transparent; paint-order: stroke fill; }
nodes.ai_tell_note: A poster device that depends on type size and weight.

nodes.name: One word in a contrasting face
nodes.what: A single word in the headline switches to a contrasting face (a serif in a grotesque line, or the mono), set roman, same size, slightly lower baseline.
nodes.implementation: span.alt { font-family: var(--pf-font-mono or a serif); font-weight 400; } keep it to one word per page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Instrument Serif italic as the accent word is a known generated-site tell; use a roman serif or the mono, once.

nodes.name: Vertical side labels
nodes.what: Section labels rotated to read bottom to top along the left gutter in mono 11px; the main column keeps a clean top edge.
nodes.implementation: writing-mode: vertical-rl; rotate: 180deg; position absolute left 0; letter-spacing .08em.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Print-derived; shows the grid has a margin column.

nodes.name: Mono index numbers
nodes.what: Every list item, figure and section carries a small mono index such as ( 01 ), 01 / 05 or Fig 2.3 at 11 to 12px with .06em tracking, in muted ink.
nodes.implementation: font-family var(--pf-font-mono); font-size 11px; letter-spacing .06em; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; colour text-muted.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on 17 of 47 admired sites; it signals the page was laid out, not generated.

nodes.name: Tight display type
nodes.what: Display lines at letter-spacing -0.04 to -0.06em and line-height .85 to .92, so a two-line headline forms a block; body stays at default tracking.
nodes.implementation: h1 { letter-spacing: -.05em; line-height: .88; text-wrap: balance; } only above 48px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Templates leave display tracking at 0 or -0.02; the tight block is a typographic decision.

nodes.name: Bracket button
nodes.what: Buttons and links set in mono inside square brackets, [ Get started ], no fill and no border; hover swaps the brackets to filled bars.
nodes.implementation: a::before content '[ '; a::after content ' ]'; font-family mono; hover changes bracket colour to primary; focus ring stays visible.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Terminal and hardware brands; unmistakably chosen.

nodes.name: Fill-up hover button
nodes.what: An outlined button whose fill rises from the bottom on hover over 300ms while the label inverts; the pressed state drops the fill by 2px.
nodes.implementation: A ::before layer with scaleY from 0 to 1, transform-origin bottom, ease-out; label colour via color-mix; reduced motion swaps instantly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A studio hover that depends on the outline treatment.

nodes.name: Pill with circled icon
nodes.what: A pill button whose label sits left and whose icon lives in a filled circle at the right end; on hover the circle grows to fill the pill and the icon turns 45 degrees.
nodes.implementation: Flex pill; the icon wrapper 32px circle in on-primary over primary; transition transform 250ms; icon from the direction's icon set.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Widespread on Framer templates; fine on soft and playful products, avoid elsewhere.

nodes.name: Offset underline links
nodes.what: Links and secondary actions are plain text with a 1px underline offset by .2em that thickens or shifts colour on hover; no arrows, no chevrons.
nodes.implementation: text-decoration-thickness 1px; text-underline-offset .2em; hover text-decoration-color primary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The measured default on handmade product sites.

nodes.name: Line mask reveal
nodes.what: On load, each line of the headline rises into view through its own overflow mask, 700 to 900ms, staggered 80ms per line, with a quintic ease-out; nothing else on the page animates.
nodes.implementation: Wrap lines in spans inside overflow:hidden parents; animation translateY(110%) to 0; cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); prefers-reduced-motion fades instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Once, on the hero only; the measured norm on studio sites.

nodes.name: Custom cursor dot and ring
nodes.what: An 8px dot that tracks the pointer exactly and a 32px ring that follows with lag; over links the ring grows to 56px and the system cursor is hidden; disabled on touch and under reduced motion.
nodes.implementation: Two fixed divs updated from pointermove with requestAnimationFrame and lerp .15; cursor: none on html when active; pointer: fine media query gate.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Studio sites only; on a SaaS site it reads as decoration.

nodes.name: Magnetic buttons
nodes.what: Primary buttons translate up to 8px toward the pointer when it is within 40px and spring back on leave.
nodes.implementation: pointermove on a wrapper computes the offset; transform translate with a 150ms ease-out; spring back with cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); skip on touch.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Studio and portfolio sites; keep to one or two buttons.

nodes.name: Preloader counter
nodes.what: A full-screen curtain in the ink colour with a 0 to 100 counter in mono at the bottom left for about 1.2 seconds, then the curtain lifts and the hero lines reveal.
nodes.implementation: A fixed div; counter via requestAnimationFrame eased; curtain translateY(-100%) 600ms ease-in-out; only once per session (sessionStorage); never under reduced motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Showcase level only; on a product site it is a delay.

nodes.name: Count-up numerals
nodes.what: Figures count from 0 to their value once when they enter the viewport, 900ms with an ease-out, in tabular numerals so the layout does not jitter.
nodes.implementation: IntersectionObserver once; requestAnimationFrame interpolation; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; reduced motion shows the final value.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only on real figures.

nodes.name: Hover image swap
nodes.what: A product or project image swaps to its second shot on hover or focus with a 150ms crossfade; on touch the second shot is reachable by a swipe.
nodes.implementation: Two stacked images; opacity transition; the second has loading lazy; focus-visible triggers the same.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The commerce standard; honest when both images exist.

nodes.name: Scroll progress hairline
nodes.what: A 1px line at the very top of the viewport that grows with reading progress in the primary colour.
nodes.implementation: animation-timeline: scroll() on a fixed 1px div with transform scaleX from 0 to 1; transform-origin left; fallback none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Content and documentation pages; invisible until it is useful.

nodes.name: Cross-page view transitions
nodes.what: Navigating between pages crossfades the page and morphs the shared wordmark and the clicked title into place over 250 to 350ms.
nodes.implementation: @view-transition { navigation: auto; } with view-transition-name on the wordmark and the title; reduced motion sets animation none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invisible craft; no generated site sets it up.

nodes.name: Dithered imagery
nodes.what: Photographs and artwork are rendered with ordered dithering (a 4x4 Bayer matrix) in two palette colours, bg and text or primary, so imagery becomes part of the type system.
nodes.implementation: A canvas or SVG filter pipeline; in a static draft the art module draws a dithered gradient; keep source images high contrast.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A 2024 to 2026 developer-brand device (Vercel Ship, Basement); rare and specific.

nodes.name: ASCII field artwork
nodes.what: Hero artwork is a field of mono characters whose density maps to a shape or a slow wave; characters are drawn from a small set (., :, +, #) in text colour at 40 percent and primary at the peaks.
nodes.implementation: SVG text rows or a pre element; in production a canvas sampling an image or noise; 12px mono; animation optional at motion level 3.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A terminal and developer-tool signature that stock imagery cannot imitate.

nodes.name: Duotone imagery
nodes.what: Photographs mapped to two palette colours (shadows in ink, highlights in bg or primary) so every image sits in the palette; colour returns on hover where it matters.
nodes.implementation: A greyscale filter and mix-blend-mode multiply over a primary surface, or an SVG feComponentTransfer; hover removes the filter over 200ms.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A tonal decision applied to real photography.

nodes.name: Captioned figures
nodes.what: Every image or artwork carries a caption in mono with a figure number and a short true statement of what it shows; captions sit under or beside the figure, never over it.
nodes.implementation: figure and figcaption; figcaption mono 11px muted with a hairline above; numbering by section.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on Linear, Stripe Press, documentation; the opposite of a floating screenshot.

nodes.name: Rotated stickers
nodes.what: Short true labels (new, 2026, v2, open source) drawn as stickers with thick outlines and a hard shadow, rotated 4 to 12 degrees, placed on artwork or at a section corner.
nodes.implementation: Inline-block with border 2px text colour, box-shadow 4px 4px 0 text, rotate var(--r); never more than three per page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Brutalist and playful brands only; honest words on them.

nodes.name: Colour-blocked sections
nodes.what: Consecutive full-bleed sections in different solid palette colours (bg, primary with on-primary text, ink with bg text); the nav inverts over each block; no gradients anywhere.
nodes.implementation: Each section sets its own --pf-color-text and background from the palette roles; nav uses mix-blend-mode difference or a class toggled by IntersectionObserver.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Colour as structure instead of decoration; templates use one background.

nodes.name: Inverted closing section
nodes.what: The last call to action and the footer sit on an ink background with bg-coloured text, so the page closes with weight.
nodes.implementation: Wrapper sets background text colour and color bg; all tokens swapped by a data-theme attribute on that wrapper.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A composed ending; templates fade out into a sitemap.

nodes.name: One hot colour
nodes.what: Near-black ink, an off-white paper and one saturated colour (international orange, acid green, cobalt, signal red) used on under 5 percent of the page: one button, one rule, one word.
nodes.implementation: primary is the hot colour; accent equals primary; every other role is a neutral; audit the page for primary coverage.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Discipline about coverage is what reads as designed.

nodes.name: Hanging punctuation
nodes.what: Opening quotation marks and bullets hang into the margin so the text edge stays straight.
nodes.implementation: hanging-punctuation: first allow-end; text-indent -0.4em fallback for blockquotes.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A typesetting detail no template ships.

nodes.name: Tabular numerals everywhere
nodes.what: Every number that could change (prices, counts, dates, times, versions) is set in tabular numerals so columns and counters never shift.
nodes.implementation: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on tables, stats, time, prices and nav meta.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on every admired product site.

nodes.name: Plain one-line bar
nodes.what: One line: the wordmark left, three to four text links right, one quiet action; no logo mark, no button fill, 56px tall, hairline under it only after scrolling.
nodes.implementation: Flex row; links at 14px in text-muted turning text on hover; the border-bottom toggled by a scroll class or a scroll-driven animation.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Reads as default only when combined with a centred hero and a filled button; fine with any distinct hero.
